Masked immigration officers have detained two people on a crowded airport jetway bridge in
Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. As people were boarding a flight, Washington Governor Bob
Ferguson was outraged after seeing a video of the arrests.
The video is horrific and it is chilling. Masked agents who do not identify themselves
drag screaming individuals off a jetway as they're about to do something very ordinary in our country,
board a flight. The video of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person as a
woman screamed that her daughter was being taken and that she has a work permit. ICE released a
statement saying its officers were conducting a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo
Lirondo Mendoza, an immigrant from Mexico who quote "overstayed his visa in violation of our
nation's laws." President Trump says he is open to working with Democrats on one issue impacting
Americans. Those high rates on credit cards. President Trump says he is open to working with
Democrats in the new Congress to cap credit card interest rates. Trump has pushed for a 10% cap.
In an interview with Fox News on Saturday, the president said credit card companies are getting
too much. Some people say it's not free enterprise. But what's free enterprise? When you're sitting
home and you get a bill that some guy set up in an office on parking avenue and they said let's
charge a fee that's to us. So I'm all for that. Interest rates for credit cards are nearly 22%.
Democrats, including Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren, have said they are ready to
work with Trump to cap interest rates. Chantalice Duster, NPR News. The agrochemical company Bayer
has agreed to pay billions of dollars to people who sued the company alleging the weed killer
Roundup caused their cancer. NPR's Will Stone has the story. Bayer could pay as much as seven and
a quarter billion dollars in the coming years. That money will go to people who already have
non-Hodgkin lymphoma or get diagnosed in the future. In a statement, the CEO of Bayer called
the settlement a decisive milestone that will mitigate pending and future litigation.
The World Health Organization's cancer agency has found that glyphosate, the main ingredient in the
company's weed killer Roundup, is probably carcinogenic to humans. Prominent scientists
in the field of environmental health have echoed those concerns. But the company denies this is the
case and the Environmental Protection Agency has also said it does not pose a risk to human health
though the agency is currently reevaluating that finding. Will Stone, NPR News. At least 11 people
have been killed in a burst of violence in Mexico's Sinaloa state after Mexican authorities captured
a cartel boss known as El Chapo Isidro. Mexico's defense cabinet says seven alleged cartel
gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed in a fierce firefight. You're listening to NPR News.
Women are more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease than men. NPR's Ping Wang reports
new research suggests changes during menopause may contribute. In midlife, most women stop
getting their periods. The transition comes with fluctuating hormones which affect parts
of the brain involved in memory. Stephanie Perez, a researcher at the University of Texas at San
Antonio, says in normal aging the brain compensates to spine. But when you have these different
genetic risk factors, not only for Alzheimer's disease but even for psychiatric illnesses,
when you go through the transition you're just more at risk. In mice, Perez and her colleagues
found that a predisposition to Alzheimer's meant more risk for cognitive decline. They think it's
related to hormonal changes and are now looking into which ones and how they affect risks.
She says current hormone replacement therapies, which tamp down on hot flashes,
are not universally helpful with cognitive deficits. The research was presented at the
Society for Neuroscience conference. Ping Wang, NPR News. A pair of spacecraft slipped into
orbit around Mercury Saturday. After an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system, the linked
spacecraft, one European, the other Japanese, will separate from one another next month and
then will map Mercury from different angles and different altitudes as part of a $2 billion
mission called Bebe Colombo. This is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury and the first
in more than a decade to the sun's closest planet. Mercury is barely bigger than the Earth's moon.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington. This message comes from Jerry. Don't overpay
